data.name: Agniraaj
data.gender_notes: Agniraaj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Agniraaj is derived from Agni, the god of fire, and Raja, the king. In Hindu mythology, Agniraaj represents the king of the fire gods. The name Agniraaj carries the meaning “Fire King” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Agniraaj usually hope their child will grow to embody fire king and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Agniraaj belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fire King.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Agniraaj total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Agniraaj holds a significant cultural impact as it is associated with the powerful god of fire, Agni. Agniraaj is believed to symbolize the strength and energy of the god Agni. In Hindu rituals, fire is an essential element, and using Agniraaj name for children may be considered a symbolic way to bestow upon them the fiery qualities and inner strength that are attributed to the god Agni.
data.spiritual_significance: Agniraaj has profound spiritual significance as it is considered a divine name that connects the individual to the divine fire god, Agni. The name embodies the qualities of purity, courage, and strength associated with Agni. Hindus believe that invoking the name of the deity through the name Agniraaj offers protection, prosperity, and spiritual guidance in life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Agniraaj: The fiery king, ruling over the primal energy of agni (fire), embodying courage, strength, and the transformative power of purification.

vedic_reference.note: Refers to Agni, the Hindu god of fire.

historical_references.reference: The name Agniraj is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. Agniraj was a powerful and fierce warrior, who was a descendant of the god of fire, Agni. He was a commander in the army of the Pandava brothers, and is remembered for his bravery and strategic skills.

Another reference to Agniraj can be found in the Puranas, a collection of ancient Indian texts. Agniraj is described as a great sage and a devotee of Lord Shiva. He is said to have performed a great penance to please the god, and was granted the boon of invincibility.
